liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Tomorrow Is Forever** (1 review): This was one of the last times the band performed this song, which Garcia favored for its structure [21]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): The performance of He's Gone is described as fantastic by the listener [27]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): The extended Truckin' jam is highlighted as a major moment of the performance [26]

## The recordings

- **gd1974-10-19.176649.sony.ecm250.falanga.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 34 songs; 214 min [1]
- **gd1974-10-19.sbd.boswell-smith.116341.flac24**: soundboard; 32 songs; 213 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [3]
- **gd1974-10-19.169824.aud.Connor.gems.flac2496**: audience recording; 32 songs; 223 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [4]
- **gd74-10-19.sbd.miller.21927.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 32 songs; 211 min; rated 4.48/5 by 33 [6]. Said about its sound: Listener claims this recording sounds superior to the multitrack soundboard available on the site; Upper frequencies are clipped and distorted, while the multitrack version sounds more musical and present; Vocals, Garcia's guitar, and piano are upfront, making singers sound very close to the listener [17][19][21][22][26][27]
- **gd1974-10-19.sbd.dfinney.228.shnf**: soundboard; 31 songs; 206 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [11]

## Around the show

- Ned Lagin plays electric piano and synthesizer during the Phil & Ned jam between sets [4]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1974-10-19.176649.sony.ecm250.falanga.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Louis Falanga; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Louis Falanga's Master Audience Cassettes; Sony ECM 250 mic > Sony TC-110 (Maxell UD C120) [1]. Also: Sony ECM 22p source supplies crowd noise and patches for Beast It On Down The Line [1]
- **gd1974-10-19.sbd.boswell-smith.116341.flac24**: taped by Will Boswell; transferred by Matt Smith; source: Lineage:16 track "truck monitor mix">2 track mixdown reel(Garcia's)>R @ 3 3/4 ips.>FLAC Transferred by: Matt Smith [3]. Also: This reel is part of the Debbie Stash, recorded in 1979 [3]
- **gd1974-10-19.169824.aud.Connor.gems.flac2496**: taped by Charlie Connor; transferred by Transferred and mastered by Jim Blackwood Speed/pitch adjusted by Jason Chastain Minor repairs, track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: Sony ECM-22P mic (mono) > Sony TC-55 > Maxell UD C-90 cassettes [4]. Also: Charles Conner provided master cassettes; Steve in Berkeley provided a first-generation reel-to-reel [4]
- **gd74-10-19.sbd.miller.21927.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [6]. Also: The show is famous for its Eyes of the World, which appeared in The Grateful Dead Movie [28]
- **gd1974-10-19.sbd.dfinney.228.shnf**: transferred by D. Finney; source: Soundboard [11]. Also: Owsley Stanley claimed no soundboard existed during these retirement concerts, complicating recording origins [11]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Winterland Arena - October 20, 1974](https://www.dead.net/show/october-20-1974) [30]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Winterland Arena - October 20, 1974](https://www.dead.net/show/october-20-1974) [31]
